source.title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology

accepted.question_text: Is the observed Higgs boson h—the scalar discovered by ATLAS and CMS whose measured properties are currently consistent with the Standard Model Higgs boson—the only scalar degree of freedom in the electroweak sector? More concretely, does h originate purely from an SU(2) gauge doublet, and if more than one Higgs doublet or other scalar field exists, is h exactly aligned with the vacuum-expectation-value direction v rather than mixed with additional scalar degrees of freedom?

evidence.quote:
Here is a list of seven open questions at the forefront of particle physics and cosmology, to which the Higgs program may provide answers:
1. Is h the only scalar degree of freedom?

The scalar h discovered in the ATLAS and CMS experiments [ 1, 2] has measured properties that are all consistent,
within present experimental accuracy, with the SM predictions for the Higgs boson [ 28]. The question that is being
asked is whether the observed Higgs boson is the SM Higgs boson. In fact, one can separate this question to two:
1. Does h originate from purely a doublet?
2. If there is more than a single doublet, is h in exactly the direction of v?

accepted.question_text: Are there light degrees of freedom that are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group, especially states related to dark matter, and can the Higgs sector reveal or constrain them? A concrete version asks whether adding a real scalar field S(x) in the gauge-singlet representation (1,1)_0, possibly mixing with the Higgs field or appearing in Higgs decays such as h → SS when kinematically allowed, describes new light physics accessible to Higgs measurements.

accepted.question_text: What is the solution to the flavor puzzles in particle physics: why the charged fermion masses and CKM mixing angles have small, hierarchical structure; why neutrino-related flavor parameters appear not to show comparable hierarchy, degeneracy, or smallness; and, if there is TeV-scale new physics, what alignment or degeneracy mechanism prevents it from producing large deviations in flavor-changing neutral current processes? Can measurements of Higgs Yukawa couplings and flavor-violating Higgs-related processes distinguish among proposed solutions?
accepted.context_brief: Flavor puzzles and Higgs Yukawa measurements

evidence.quote:
Here is a list of seven open questions at the forefront of particle physics and cosmology, to which the Higgs program may provide answers:
7. What is the solution of the ﬂavor puzzle(s)?

IV. WHAT IS THE SOLUTION OF THE FLA VOR PUZZLE(S)?
There are several reasons that make the study of ﬂavor physics via Higgs physics well motivated. First, ﬂavor
physics raises three puzzles [ 30]:
• The Standard Model ﬂavor puzzle: Why is there structure (smallne ss and hierarchy) in the charged fermion
masses and the CKM mixing angles?
• The neutrino ﬂavor puzzle: Why, in contrast to the charged fermio ns, there seems to be no structure (neither
hierarchy nor degeneracy nor smallness) in the neutrino-related ﬂ avor parameters?
• The new physics ﬂavor puzzle: If there is new physics at the TeV sca le, what is the mechanism (alignment
and/or degeneracy) that prevents it from signiﬁcantly modifying t he SM predictions for ﬂavor changing neutral
current processes?

Various models have been suggested to answer one or more of thes e questions. The best hope to make further
progress is by measuring new ﬂavor parameters (beyond the matr ix elements of the CKM matrix). Measurements of
the Yukawa couplings of h provide such an opportunity.

trace.notes: Normalized arXiv abs URL to https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.00382.pdf and downloaded the readable PDF artifact.

Mapped the PDF as a 17-page review with sections: Introduction, Experiments, Singlet Scalars, Flavor Puzzles, Additional Questions, Conclusions, and References; likely open-question regions are the seven-question list on page 1, the singlet-scalar section, the flavor-puzzle section, and Section V subsections A-E.
Extracted 'Is h the only scalar degree of freedom?' from the page 1 list and merged Section V.A's two subquestions about doublet origin and alignment with v.
Extracted the Higgs-elementarity/compositeness question and supporting SILH context.
Extracted the hierarchy/naturalness question about why m_h^2 is much smaller than m_Pl^2.
Extracted the electroweak-phase-transition question and expanded the strong-first-order criterion from Section V.D.
Extracted the CP-violating-Higgs-interactions question and its baryogenesis motivation.
Extracted the light SM-singlet degrees-of-freedom question and supporting real-singlet-scalar model context.
Extracted the flavor-puzzle question and merged the three explicit flavor-puzzle bullets into one self-contained top-level item.

Rewrote all accepted candidates as self-contained questions by inlining the observed-Higgs context, scalar-sector terminology, hierarchy-problem setting, EWPT criterion, CP-violating Yukawa examples, singlet-scalar representation, and flavor-puzzle subquestions where supported by evidence.

Merged repeated formulations from the introduction, singlet-scalar section, Section V headings, and Table XI into the seven canonical top-level questions; did not create separate accepted rows for Section V.A subquestions or the three flavor-puzzle bullets because they refine q_001 and q_007 respectively.
Rejected the theory-uncertainty item because it is a measurement-systematics issue rather than one of the paper's primary open research questions.
Rejected the missing-dedicated-study item because the source states a literature gap but does not formulate a standalone open research question with enough problem content.

Accepted seven items after self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, solved-status, and schema-conformance checks; no accepted item is marked solved by the source.
